Any portion of the Torah <note>the Five Books of Moses</note> that mentions the name <term>YHVH Elohim</term> refers to actions performed through the combined attributes of the Attribute of Justice <note>Hebrew: Middat ha-Din</note> and the Attribute of Mercy <note>Hebrew: Middat ha-Rachamim</note>. You will find this regarding the creation of the first man, his judgment, his expulsion from Eden, and all those matters. You will find they were all executed through both Justice and Mercy, in perfect completeness, with Justice according to what was strictly true and Mercy according to what was appropriate.

Following this principle, the Torah states: The Rock, His work is perfect <note>Deuteronomy 32:4</note>. The explanation of the verse is this: The Rock, who decrees judgment with strength, does not act with cruelty. He does not decree judgment until His work is "perfect," meaning that the decree was first deliberated by both attributes, Loving-kindness <note>Hebrew: Chesed</note> and Justice. This is the meaning of "His work is perfect" <term>tamim</term>.

The term <term>tamim</term> <gloss>perfect/complete</gloss> is a secret referring to two things together. It is as if one said <term>te'omim</term> <gloss>twins</gloss>, but the language of honor uses the term <term>tamim</term> for these two supernal matters, while for earthly things it uses the term <term>te'omim</term>. Thus it says, and they shall be doubled <term>te'omim</term> from below, and they shall be complete <term>tamim</term> together at the top <note>Exodus 26:24</note>. Below they are "twins" because they appear as two separate things, opposites like an advocate and an accuser. But above, all is a single intention. Between the advocate and the accuser, both share one purpose. There is no hatred or love there, and no partiality, only true judgment. Therefore it says "His work is perfect," meaning He consulted Justice and Mercy and then decreed the judgment. This is the secret of "True Judgment."

Regarding the phrase, for all His ways are justice <note>Deuteronomy 32:4</note>, it means this is evident to every observer. You already know that <term>Mishpat</term> <gloss>Justice/Judgment</gloss> is comprised of both Justice and Mercy. <term>Mishpat</term> corresponds to Jacob, who is the Middle Pillar, balancing between the two "tents" of Abraham and Isaac. Abraham corresponds to Loving-kindness, Isaac corresponds to Justice, and Jacob decides between them: a plain man <term>ish tam</term>, dwelling in tents <note>Genesis 25:27</note>. <term>Mishpat</term> corresponds to Jacob, drawing from the Loving-kindness of Abraham's side and the Justice of Isaac's side. Thus it says, You have executed justice <term>mishpat</term> and righteousness <term>tzedakah</term> in Jacob <note>Psalm 99:4</note>.

The Prophet said: O Lord <term>YHVH</term>, correct me, but with justice <term>mishpat</term>; not in Your anger, lest You bring me to nothing <note>Jeremiah 10:24</note>. The explanation is: "Correct me, Lord, but with justice," where the word "but" <term>ach</term> implies a partition—meaning, through the half of the attribute of Justice that is Mercy. Since <term>Mishpat</term> is half Justice and half Mercy, he says "but with justice" and follows with "not in Your anger," revealing the secret of diminishing the half of Justice that stems from "Anger."

Therefore, <term>Mishpat</term> depends on Jacob, who is the "Father of the Tribes." Having known the great pain of children, when the Holy One decrees upon them, Jacob seeks mercy and righteousness for them. The secret is: And the Lord of Hosts shall be exalted in justice <note>Isaiah 5:16</note>. What is written immediately after? And God the Holy One is sanctified in righteousness. This means when the Judgment is collected, the Justice rests and turns toward the attribute of <term>El</term> <gloss>God</gloss>. This is the secret of "And God the Holy One is sanctified in righteousness." Whenever the name <term>YHVH Tzevaot</term> is exalted in justice, the attribute of <term>El</term>, which is higher, arrives and performs righteousness, and Justice is served. This is the secret of the saying that <term>Mishpat</term> is included in Loving-kindness and Justice.

There is a great secret in the verse: Righteousness <term>Tzedek</term> and Justice <term>Mishpat</term> are the foundation of Your throne <note>Psalm 89:15</note>. Sometimes <term>Tzedek</term> <gloss>Righteousness</gloss> acts as strict Justice depending on how the flow is received, for <term>Tzedek</term> can be a harsh judgment in its strength. However, when <term>Mishpat</term> is partnered with it, the Throne is established with Mercy. And if it is exalted through <term>Mishpat</term> and reaches the point where Loving-kindness and Truth meet, they are called "The Shining Face." Then everything becomes great Mercy, and this is the secret of "shall go before

->Your Face<-

<meta>Commentary section</meta>

This hints at "The Lord our God, the Lord is One." They have one single intention. The essence and refinement of it is the distribution of Justice and Kindness according to the recipients who are prepared for them through spiritual awakening. In the Zohar <note>Parashat Balak</note> it is discussed how the Ancient of Ancients <term>Atika de-Atikin</term> is entirely white <note>pure mercy</note>. When everything is unified, everything becomes life. Everything is balanced before the paths separate to the right and left. From our side, Justice appears, but the secret of Justice is surrendered to the Holy Head. It is written, "The voice of the Lord is upon the waters." This means all His ways are <term>Mishpat</term>. <term>Mishpat</term> is a revealed way, visible to all below, whereas supernal matters may be hidden. Thus it is written regarding Job, that he spoke without knowledge. The explanation is that the secret was revealed to him only in part, as the sages said. The attribute of Justice is gathered under the hand of Loving-kindness, included within it as a foundation.

<summary>This page explains the synthesis of Justice (Din) and Mercy (Rachamim) in the divine name YHVH Elohim and the concept of Mishpat (Justice/Balance). It links these attributes to the patriarchs Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, establishing Jacob as the balancing middle pillar.</summary>
<keywords>Justice, Mercy, Mishpat, Jacob, Abraham, Isaac, Tamim, Sephirot, Zohar, Divine Names</keywords>

A section that mentions the name <term>YHVH Elohim</term> indicates actions performed through all the <term>middot</term> <gloss>divine attributes</gloss> which are completed by the attribute of Justice and the attribute of Mercy. You find this in the creation of the first man, in his judgment, and in his expulsion. In all these matters, you will find they occurred through both Justice and Mercy, everything in complete perfection, with Mercy and Justice applied as appropriate in true judgment.

Based on this principle, the Torah states: The Rock, His work is perfect <note>Deuteronomy 32:4; original: Ha-Tzur Tamim Pe'alo</note>. The explanation of the verse is as follows: The Rock who decrees judgment with strength does not act with cruelty. He does not decree judgment until His work is perfect, meaning the judgment He decreed was first deliberated between the two attributes of Loving-kindness <note>Chesed</note> and Justice <note>Din</note>. This is the meaning of "His work is perfect" <term>tamim</term>. For the term <term>tamim</term> <gloss>perfect/complete</gloss> is the secret of two things. It is as if one said <term>te'umim</term> <gloss>twins</gloss>, but out of respect for the two supernal matters, the term <term>tamim</term> is used, while below, the term <term>te'umim</term> is used.

As it is said: And they shall be coupled <term>te'umim</term> <gloss>twins</gloss> from below, and they shall be complete <term>tamim</term> <gloss>perfect</gloss> together at the top <note>Exodus 26:24</note>. Below they are <term>te'umim</term>, above they are <term>tamim</term>. This is because below they appear as two distinct things, a thing and its opposite, like an advocate and an accuser. But above, all is one intention. Both the advocate and the accuser have a single purpose; there is no hatred or love there, and no favoritism, only true judgment. Therefore it says "His work is perfect," for He consulted with Justice and Mercy and then decreed the judgment. This is the secret of true judgment.

Regarding the phrase "for all His ways are justice," this means it is visible to the eyes of all who see, as it says "for all His ways are justice." You already know that Justice <term>Mishpat</term> is comprised of Justice <term>Din</term> and Mercy <term>Rachamim</term>. For <term>Mishpat</term> corresponds to Jacob, who is the Middle Line <note>the central pillar of the Sefirot</note> that balances between the two tents of Abraham and Isaac. Abraham corresponds to Loving-kindness <note>Chesed</note> and Isaac corresponds to Justice <note>Din</note>. Jacob decides between them: a plain man <term>ish tam</term>, dwelling in tents <note>Genesis 25:27</note>. And <term>Mishpat</term> corresponds to Jacob, drawing from Loving-kindness on the side of Abraham and from Justice on the side of Isaac. Thus it says: You have executed justice <term>mishpat</term> and righteousness <term>tzedakah</term> in Jacob <note>Psalm 99:4</note>.

The prophet said: O Lord <term>YHVH</term>, correct me, but with justice <term>mishpat</term>; not in Your anger, lest You bring me to nothing <note>Jeremiah 10:24</note>. The explanation of the verse "correct me, Lord, but with justice" uses the word "but" <term>ach</term> to denote a part, as if to say: with half of the attribute of Justice, which is Loving-kindness. For <term>Mishpat</term> is half Justice and half Loving-kindness. Therefore he said "but with justice" and followed with "not in Your anger," revealing the secret of diminishing the half of Justice that comes from the side of Anger.

Therefore <term>Mishpat</term> depends on Jacob, who is the "father" among the tribes. He knew the great pain of children; when the Holy One, blessed be He, decrees upon them, Jacob seeks mercy and righteousness for them. The secret is: And the Lord of hosts is exalted through justice <note>Isaiah 5:16</note>. What is written afterward? And the holy God is sanctified through righteousness. This means when Justice is exalted, the harsh decree rests and turns toward the attribute of <term>El</term>, which is the secret of "And the holy God <term>ha-El</term> is sanctified through righteousness." Generally, when the Lord of hosts is exalted through justice, the attribute of <term>El</term> arrives from above and performs righteousness, and justice is served. This is the secret of what they said: Justice <term>Mishpat</term> is included in Loving-kindness and Justice <term>Din</term>, and "You have executed justice and righteousness in Jacob."

The great secret is: Righteousness <term>Tzedek</term> and justice <term>mishpat</term> are the foundation of Your throne <note>Psalm 89:15</note>. For <term>Tzedek</term> is sometimes Justice according to its reception of flow, as I explained that <term>Tzedek</term> is a great and strong justice. But when <term>Mishpat</term> is joined with it, then the Throne is established with Mercy. And if it is exalted through Justice and reaches until Loving-kindness and Truth together, they are called the "Radiant Face." Then everything becomes great Mercy. This is the secret of: shall go before

-> Your face <-

This alludes to: The Lord our God, the Lord is one. They have a single intention, for the ultimate purpose and essence is the division of Justice and Loving-kindness according to the recipients who are prepared for them through awakening. In the <term>Zohar</term> <gloss>The Book of Radiance</gloss>, in the section on Balak, it says that the Ancient of Ancients is entirely white, and everything is life, everything is one. It describes the arrangement of the right side and the left side, where Justice is balanced. From our side, these are separated into the paths of the right and the left to support the judgment. <summary>This page explains how the divine attribute of Justice (Mishpat) is a balance between harsh Judgment (Din) and Loving-kindness (Chesed). It uses the patriarchs Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob to illustrate these forces and explores the linguistic connection between perfection and twins.</summary>

A portion in which the name <term>YHVH Elohim</term> is mentioned indicates they are performed through all the attributes that are completed by the Attribute of Justice and the Attribute of Mercy. You will find this in the creation of the first man, in his judgment, and in his expulsion, and in all those matters. You will find that they all came about through the Attribute of Justice and the Attribute of Mercy, and everything was in perfect completion through mercy and justice, all according to what is fitting in true judgment. And according to this principle, the Torah said: The Rock, His work is perfect. And the explanation of the verse is this: The Rock who decrees judgment with strength does not act with cruelty; He does not decree judgment except that His work is perfect, meaning that the judgment He decreed previously was deliberated upon by the two attributes: Lovingkindness and Justice. And this is His work is perfect. For the term <term>Tamim</term> [perfect] is the secret of two things, and it is as if it said <term>Teumim</term> [twins], except that in the language of honor it speaks of two things on high using the term <term>Tamim</term>, and below it uses the term <term>Teumim</term>. And so it says: and they shall be doubled [<term>Teumim</term>] from below together they shall be whole [<term>Tamim</term>] at its top. Below they are twins, above they are perfect, because below they appear as two things, a thing and its opposite, like a supporter and an accuser; but above, everything is one intention. Whether it is the supporter or the accuser, they both have one intention, and there is no hatred or love there, and there is no favoritism there, but rather true judgment. Therefore it said, His work is perfect: through justice and mercy He deliberated and decreed the judgment, and this is the secret of true judgment. And as for what it said, for all His ways are justice, the explanation is that everything is before the eye of every observer, as it says: for all His ways are justice. And you already know that Justice is included in Judgment and Mercy, for Justice corresponds to Jacob, who is the Middle Pillar that mediates between the two tents which are Abraham and Isaac. Abraham corresponds to Lovingkindness, Isaac corresponds to Judgment, and Jacob decides between them: a perfect man, dwelling in tents. And Justice corresponds to Jacob, drawing from Lovingkindness from the side of Abraham and from Judgment from the side of Isaac. And so it says: Justice and righteousness in Jacob You have made. And the prophet said: Correct me, O <term>YHVH</term>, but with justice, not in Your anger, lest You bring me to nothing. And the explanation of the verse Correct me, O <term>YHVH</term>, but with justice: what it said <term>Ach</term> [but] is a division, as if to say, with half the attribute of Justice, which is Lovingkindness, for Justice is half Judgment and half Lovingkindness. Therefore it said, but with justice, and said afterward, not in Your anger, lest You bring me to nothing, and it revealed the secret to diminish the half of Justice that comes from the side of anger. Therefore, Justice is dependent on Jacob, who is the father among the tribes; he knew the great pain of children when the Holy One, Blessed be He, decrees upon them, so that he would seek mercy and righteousness for them. And the secret of And <term>YHVH</term> of Hosts shall be exalted in justice: what is written after it? And the holy God is sanctified in righteousness. That is to say, when Justice is exalted, Judgment rests and turns to the attribute of <term>El</term>, which is the secret of what is said: And the holy God is sanctified in righteousness. Generally, when <term>YHVH</term> of Hosts is exalted in justice, the attribute of <term>El</term> comes, which is above, and performs righteousness and sweetens the Justice. And this is the secret of what they said: and Justice is included in Lovingkindness and Judgment, and it says: Justice and righteousness in Jacob You have made. And the great secret: Righteousness and justice are the foundation of Your throne, for <term>Tzedek</term> [Righteousness] is at times Judgment according to its reception of flow, as I explained that <term>Tzedek</term> is a great judgment in its strength. But when Justice is associated with it, then the throne is established in mercy. And if it is exalted in justice, and reaches until Lovingkindness and Truth together, they are called the Shining Face, then everything is made into great mercies, and this is the secret of [they] shall go before

They have one intention, for its purpose and essence is the distribution of Judgment and Lovingkindness according to the recipients who are prepared for them through arousal. And in the Book of the <term>Zohar</term>, portion of Balak: everything is the Ancient of Ancients... everything is weighed before all... separating to the paths of the right to support the judgment, and from our side they were... for Justice is the secret... handed over to the holy head... and it is written: The voice of <term>YHVH</term> is upon the waters... as if to say, for all His ways are justice. כי כבר ראיתי המלכיות שהם רמז לז' מלכיות. וס' כן מה אלה לחיות ענין לחיותי בהם :

וַיַּעַן הַמַּלְאָךְ וַיֹּאמֶר אֵלַי אֵלֶּה אַרְבַּע רוּחוֹת הַשָּׁמַיִם יוֹצְאוֹת מֵהִתְיַצֵּב עַל־אֲדוֹן כָּל־הָאָרֶץ : אֲשֶׁר־בָּהּ הַסּוּסִים הַשְּׁחֹרִים יֹצְאִים אֶל־אֶרֶץ צָפוֹן וְהַלְּבָנִים יָצְאוּ אֶל־אַחֲרֵיהֶם וְהַבְּרֻדִּים יָצְאוּ אֶל־אֶרֶץ הַתֵּימָן : וְהָאֲמֻצִּים יָצָאוּ וַיְבַקְשׁוּ לָלֶכֶת לְהִתְהַלֵּךְ בָּאָרֶץ וַיֹּאמֶר לְכוּ הִתְהַלְּכוּ בָאָרֶץ וַתִּתְהַלַּכְנָה בָאָרֶץ: וַיַּזְעֵק אֹתִי וַיְדַבֵּר אֵלַי לֵאמֹר רְאֵה הַיּוֹצְאִים אֶל־אֶרֶץ צָפוֹן הֵנִיחוּ אֶת־רוּחִי בְּאֶרֶץ צָפוֹן :

**ויען .** אלה ארבע רוחות. כמו לז' רוחי' . וכן ויבא ירושלם כמו לירושלם. ד"א לז' בן שחור כמו לבן שחור. והדומיו לו. לז' חלק הד' מרכבות ויוצאות לז' רוחות שמואל ב' י' השמים. כלז' לתת רשות לז' מלכיות למשול בז' רוחות כל אחת בזמנה . כלז' בכל העולם שהוז' ל' עזות : מהתיצב על אדון כל הארץ. כלז' בשליחות האל ששלטם על זה . כמו עומר ויבחו בני האלהים להתיצב על ה' : <margin>איוב ב'</margin> **אשר בה .** השחורים . ולז' זכר השחורים כי כבר עבר עתק מלכות בבל . ומלכות מדי ופרס יחיו תחלה אל ארץ צפון שהיו בכל להשחיתה וחח"כ משלו בכל ממלכות הארץ: והלבני' שהוז' מלכות יון יצאו אל אחריה' שהמלכות נברק . שהיו אלכסנדרוס מקדון המלך הראשון ליון הרג דריוש בבבל ולקח המלוכה ממנו ומלך וח"כ קוז וקכחיס חחריו בכל העולם : **והברודי' יצאו אל ארץ התימן .** שהיו חלק קדוס כעבור כי רומי היא שנונית ויוכיחום קיסר שמלך על רומי החל להלחם במלכות יון ובתחילת מלחמותיו יצא אל ארץ מצרים שהיא דרומית ובכל הארצות היו מולכים בני יון חז . וזק ויוכיחום קיסר התגבר עליהם והוז' העביר המלוכה מבני יון והחזירה לרומיים : **והאמוצים .** הם רמז למלכות ישמעאל שהתחמט מעצמם לבקש מלוכה לחיות מקום שיהיה לשיכך לז' קתר להם רוח . וזהו שאמר ויבקשו ללכת להתהלך בארץ : **ויאמר .** כלומר נתן להם רשות להתהלך ולכבוש ארצות : **ויזעק .** כלומ' קרא עלי בקול גדול וחמר לי **ראה היוצאים אל ארץ צפון הניחו את רוחי בארץ צפון** כלומר חלק השחורים שיצאו אל בבל להשחיתה

I have already seen that the visions represent the four monarchies; if so, what are these? for what purpose do I see them?
“And the angel answered ——— These the four winds of heaven”—Winds רוחות here signifies the same as לרוחות to the winds. (There are similar cases where the preposition ל, to, is omitted,) as ויבא ירושלם, “And he came Jerusalem,” i.e., to Jerusalem. (1 Kings iii. 15.) And again: בן שאול, “the son of Saul,” for לבן שאול, “to the son of Saul” (2 Sam. iv. 2); and other similar cases. The meaning is, These four chariots go forth to the four winds of heaven; i.e., to give permission to the four monarchies to rule in the four winds, each in its time, that is to say, in the whole world, which has four corners.
“From standing before the Lord of the whole earth,” i.e., commissioned by God, who sent them, according as it is said, “And the sons of God came to present themselves before the Lord.” (Job i. 6.)
“Which are therein.”—He does not mention the red horses, for the Babylonian monarchy had already passed away. The Medo-Persian monarchy went forth first to the land of the north, which is Babylon, to destroy it, but afterwards ruled over all the kingdoms of the earth. The white horses, which represent the Grecian monarchy, went forth after them, when their kingdom was strong; for behold, Alexander the Macedonian, the first King of Greece, slew Darius in Babylon, and took the kingdom from him, and afterwards had dominion, he and his successors, over the whole earth.
“And the grisled go forth toward the country of Teman,” which is the south country, for Rome is to the north, and Lulianus Cæsar, who reigned over Rome, began to wage war against the kingdom of Greece; and in the beginning of his wars, he went forth to the land of Egypt, which is to the south. At that time the Greeks ruled over all lands, but this Lulianus Cæsar prevailed against them, and caused the kingdom to pass away from the Greeks, and turned it to the Romans.
“And the bay” (strong).—These signify the Turkish empire, who strengthened themselves to seek a kingdom in any place that might offer: and therefore he does not define any wind of heaven for them. This is what is said, “And they sought to go, that they might walk to and fro through the earth.”
“And he said,” i.e., Permission was given them to walk to and fro, and to subdue lands.
“Then cried he upon me.”—He cried upon me with a loud voice, and said to me, “Behold these that go toward the north country have quieted my spirit in the north country; i.e., These black horses which went forth to Babylon to destroy it
[context] have caused a quieting of my spirit by destroying it.

For I have already seen the kingdoms, which are a hint to the seven kingdoms. And so, what are these for? To give life to the matter of my living in them.

And the angel answered and said to me: "These are the four spirits of heaven, going forth from standing before the Lord of all the earth. The one with the black horses goes forth to the north country, and the white ones go forth after them, and the spotted ones go forth to the south country." And the strong ones went forth and sought to go, to walk to and fro through the earth; and he said: "Go, walk to and fro through the earth." So they walked to and fro through the earth. Then he cried out to me and spoke to me, saying: "Behold, those who go toward the north country have quieted my spirit in the north country."

**And he answered.** These are the four spirits. Like "to the four spirits." And similarly, "and he came to Jerusalem" is like "into Jerusalem." Another interpretation: "to the son of a black man" is like "the black son." And things similar to it. This refers to the division of the four chariots, which go out to the four directions of the heavens. This is to give permission to the four kingdoms to rule in the four directions, each one in its time. This refers to the whole world, which is a place of strength. **From standing before the Lord of all the earth.** That is, on a mission from God who gave them power over this. As it says: "And the sons of God came to stand before the Lord." <margin>Job 2</margin>

The kingdoms of Media and Persia went first to the north country, for they were there to destroy it, and afterward they ruled over all the kingdoms of the earth. **And the white ones**, which are the kingdom of Greece, went out after them once the kingdom was established. For Alexander of Macedon, the first king of Greece, killed Darius in Babylon and took the kingdom from him and reigned, and afterward his successors ruled throughout the whole world.

**And the spotted ones go forth to the south country.** This refers to the Roman portion, because Rome is <term>shannunit</term> <gloss>perhaps "swallow-like" or "changing"</gloss>. Augustus Caesar, who ruled over Rome, began to fight against the kingdom of Greece. At the start of his wars, he went out to the land of Egypt, which is in the south. In those days, the sons of Greece ruled all the lands. Then Augustus Caesar overpowered them, transferred the kingdom from the sons of Greece, and returned it to the Romans.

בצדן בשובו אל נותן כתיב: כי עין בעין יראו בשוב ה' ציון: ואמר ונגלה כבוד ה' וראו כל בשר יחדו כי פי ה' דבר: אב הרחמים הוא ינחם עם עמוסים ויזכור ברית איתנים ויציל נפשותינו מן השעות הרעות ויגער ביצר הרע מן הנשאים ויחון אותנו לפליטת עולמים. וימלא משאלותינו במדת טובה ישועה ורחמים:

<image-desc size="small" type="decorative" significance="low">Decorative ornament</image-desc>

כסא דנביאין ספר מורא חופים וכו':
ואת התורה אשר שם משה לפני בני ישראל על פי ה' ביד משה:

הללו את שם ה' כי נשגב שמו לבדו:
הודו על ארץ ושמים: וירם קרן לעמו תהלה לכל חסידיו לבני ישראל עם קרובו הללויה:

ואומר בשם עומד לדור, וכתוב ול"מ ויו"ם ובזמן כנמנה לדור מעור.
כסא דנביאין פס"ק (כיכל חופים וכו'):

ובטחה ואמר שובה ה' רבבות אלפי ישראל: קומה ה' למנוחתך אתה וארון עזך: כהניך ילבשו צדק וחסידיך ירננו: בעבור דוד עבדך אל תשב פני משיחך: כי לקח טוב נתתי לכם תורתי אל תעזובו: עץ חיים היא למחזיקים בה ותומכיה מאשר: דרכיה דרכי נועם וכל נתיבותיה שלום: השיבנו ה' אליך ונשובה חדש ימינו כקדם: אשרי וכו':

למנצח מזמור לדוד: יענך ה' ביום צרה ישגבך שם אלהי יעקב: ישלח עזרך מקדש ומציון יסעדך: יזכור כל מנחותיך ועולתך ידשנה סלה: יתן לך כלבבך וכל עצתך ימלא: נרננה בישועתך ובשם אלהינו נדגול ימלא ה' כל שאלותיך: עתה ידעתי כי הושיע ה' משיחו יענהו משמי קדשו בגבורות ישע ימינו: אלה ברכב ואלה בסוסים ואנחנו בשם ה' אלהינו נזכיר: המה כרעו ונפלו ואנחנו קמנו ונתעודד: ה' הושיעה המלך יעננו ביום קראנו: ואני לציון גואל ולשבי פשע ביעקב נאם ה': ואני זאת בריתי אותם אמר ה' רוחי אשר עליך ודברי אשר שמתי בפיך לא ימושו מפיך ומפי זרעך ומפי זרע זרעך אמר ה' מעתה ועד עולם:

ואתה קדוש יושב תהלות ישראל: וקרא זה אל זה ואמר קדוש קדוש קדוש ה' צבאות מלא כל הארץ כבודו: ומקבלים דין מן דין ואמרין קדיש בשמי מרומא עלאה בית שכינתיה קדיש על ארעא עובד גבורתיה קדיש לעלם ולעלמי עלמיא: ה' צבאות מליא כל ארעא זיו יקריה: נהשאנא רוח נשמע אהקיל רעש גדול רב רבין כבוד ה' ממקומו: ונשפתני רוחא ושמעת בתרי קל זיע סגיא דמשבחין ואמרין קריה יקרא דיו מאתר בית שכינתיה: ה' לעלם ולעלמי עלמיא: יי מלכותיה קאם לעלם ולעלמי עלמיא: יי אלהי אברהם יצחק וישראל אבותינו שמרה זאת לעולם ליצר מחשבות לבב עמך והכן לבבם אליך: והוא רחום יכפר עון ולא ישחית והרבה להשיב אפו ולא יעיר כל חמתו: כי אתה אדני טוב וסלח ורב חסד לכל קוראיך: צדקתך צדק לעולם ותורתך אמת: תתן אמת ליעקב חסד לאברהם אשר נשבעת לאבותינו מימי קדם: ברוך אדני יום יום יעמס לנו האל ישועתנו סלה: ה' צבאות עמנו משגב לנו אלהי יעקב סלה: ה' צבאות אשרי אדם בוטח בך: ה' הושיעה המלך יעננו ביום קראנו: ברוך הוא אלהינו שבראנו לכבודו והבדילנו מן התועים ונתן לנו תורת אמת וחיי עולם נטע בתוכנו הוא יפתח לבנו בתורתו וישם בלבבנו אהבתו ויראתו ולעשות רצונו ולעבדו בלבב שלם למען לא ניגע לריק ולא נלד לבהלה: יהי רצון מלפניך ה' אלהינו ואלהי אבותינו שנשמור חקיך בעולם הזה ונזכה ונחיה ונראה ונירש טובה וברכה לשני ימות המשיח ולחיי העולם הבא: למען יזמרה כבוד ולא ידום ה' אלהי לעולם אודך: ברוך הגבר אשר יבטח בה' והיה ה' מבטחו: בטחו בה' עדי עד כי ביה ה' צור עולמים: ויבטחו בך יודעי שמך כי לא עזבת דורשיך ה': חפץ למען צדקו יגדיל תורה ויאדיר:

<column-break/>

יי אדונינו מה אדיר שמך בכל הארץ:
חוקו ויאמץ לבבכם כל המיחלים ליי:

ועתה יגדל נא כח אדני כאשר דברת לאמר: זכור רחמיך וחסדיך כי מעולם המה:

יתגדל ויתקדש שמה רבא. בעלמא די ברא כרעותה וימליך מלכותיה ויצמח פורקניה ויקרב [נ"א קץ] משיחיה: בחייכון וביומיכון ובחיי דכל בית ישראל בעגלא ובזמן קריב ואמרו אמן: יהא שמה רבא מברך לעלם ולעלמי עלמיא: יתברך וישתבח ויתפאר ויתרומם ויתנשא ויתהדר ויתעלה ויתהלל שמה דקודשא בריך הוא. לעילא (מפע"ם ולעילא מכל) מן כל ברכתא ושירתא תשבחתא ונחמתא דאמירן בעלמא ואמרו אמן: קבל קבל ברחמים וברצון את תפלתנו: תתקבל צלותהון ובעותהון דכל בית ישראל קדם אבוהון די בשמיא ואמרו אמן: קבל יהי שם ה' מבורך מעתה ועד עולם:

מן יהא שלמא רבא מן שמיא וחיים עלינו ועל כל ישראל ואמרו אמן: קסו עזרי מעם ה' עשה שמים וארץ: עשה שלום במרומיו הוא יעשה שלום עלינו ועל כל ישראל ואמרו אמן:

תפלה לדוד הטה ה' אזנך עני כי עני ואביון אני: שמרה נפשי כי חסיד אני הושיע עבדך אתה אלהי הבוטח אליך: חנני אדני כי אליך אקרא כל היום: שמח נפש עבדך כי אליך אדני נפשי אשא: כי אתה אדני טוב וסלח ורב חסד לכל קוראיך: האזינה ה' תפלתי והקשיבה בקול תחנוני: ביום צרתי אקראך כי תענני: אין כמוך באלהים אדני ואין כמעשיך: כל גוים אשר עשית יבואו וישתחוו לפניך אדני ויכבדו לשמך: כי גדול אתה ועושה נפלאות אתה אלהים לבדך: הורני ה' דרכך אהלך באמתך יחד לבבי ליראה שמך: אודך אדני אלהי בכל לבבי ואכבדת שמך לעולם: כי חסדך גדול עלי והצלת נפשי משאול תחתיה: אלהים זדים קמו עלי ועדת עריצים בקשו נפשי ולא שמוך לנגדם: ואתה אדני אל רחום וחנון ארך אפים ורב חסד ואמת: פנה אלי וחנני תנה עזך לעבדך והושיעה לבן אמתך: עשה עמי אות לטובה ויראו שנאי ויבשו כי אתה ה' עזרתני ונחמתני:

בית יעקב לכו ונלכה באור יי: כי כל העמים ילכו איש בשם אלהיו ואנחנו נלך בשם ה' אלהינו לעולם ועד:
יהי ה' אלהינו עמנו כאשר היה עם אבותינו אל יעזבנו ואל יטשנו: להטות לבבנו אליו ללכת בכל דרכיו ולשמור מצותיו וחקיו ומשפטיו אשר צוה את אבותינו: ויהיו דברי אלה אשר התחננתי לפני ה' קרובים אל ה' אלהינו יומם ולילה לעשות משפט עבדו ומשפט עמו ישראל דבר יום ביומו: למען דעת כל עמי הארץ כי ה' הוא האלהים אין עוד:

שיר המעלות לדוד לולי ה' שהיה לנו יאמר נא ישראל: לולי ה' שהיה לנו בקום עלינו אדם: אזי חיים בלעונו בחרות אפם בנו: אזי המים שטפונו נחלה עבר על נפשנו: אזי עבר על נפשנו המים הזדונים: ברוך ה' שלא נתננו טרף לשניהם: נפשנו כצפור נמלטה מפח יוקשים הפח נשבר ואנחנו נמלטנו: עזרנו בשם ה' עשה שמים וארץ:

[context] And may we see him, eye to eye,
when he returneth to his habitation, as it is written, For they shall see eye to eye, when the Lord returneth unto Zion. And it is said, And the glory of the Lord shall be revealed, and all flesh shall see it together ; for the mouth of the Lord hath spoken it. May the Father of mercy have mercy upon a people that have been borne by him. May he remember the covenant with the patriarchs, deliver our souls from evil hours, check the evil inclination in them that have been carried by him, grant us of his grace an everlasting deliverance, and in the attribute of his goodness fulfil our desires by salvation and mercy.
And this is the Law which Moses set before the children of Israel, according to the commandment of the Lord by the hand of Moses.
Let them praise the name of the Lord ; for his name alone is exalted : His majesty is above the earth and heaven ; and he hath lifted up a horn for his people, to the praise of all his loving ones, even of the children of Israel, the people near unto him. Praise ye the Lord.
And when it rested, he said, Return, O Lord, unto the ten thousands of the thousands of Israel. Arise, O Lord, unto thy resting place; thou, and the ark of thy strength. Let thy priests be clothed with righteousness; and let thy loving ones shout for joy. For the sake of David thy servant, turn not away the face of thine anointed. For I give you good doctrine ; forsake ye not my Law. It is a tree of life to them that grasp it, and of them that uphold it every one is rendered happy. Its ways are ways of pleasantness, and all its paths are peace. Turn thou us unto thee, O Lord, and we shall return : renew our days as of old.
For the Chief Musician. A Psalm of David. The Lord answer thee in the day of trouble ; the name of the God of Jacob set thee up on high ; send thee help from the sanctuary, and uphold thee out of Zion ; remember all thy offerings, and accept thy burnt sacrifice (Selah): grant thee thy heart's desire, and fulfil all thy purpose. We will exult in thy salvation, and in the name of our God we will set up our banners : the Lord fulfil all thy petitions. Now know I that the Lord saveth his anointed ; he will answer him from his holy heaven with the mighty saving acts of his right hand. Some trust in chariots and some in horses : but we will make mention of the name of the Lord our God. They are bowed down and fallen : but we are risen and stand upright. Save, Lord : may the King answer us on the day when we call.
And a redeemer shall come to Zion and to them that turn from transgression in Jacob, saith the Lord. And as for me, this is my covenant with them, saith the Lord : my spirit that is upon thee, and my words which I have put in thy mouth, shall not depart out of thy mouth, nor out of the mouth of thy seed, nor out of the mouth of thy seed's seed, saith the Lord, from henceforth and for ever. But thou art holy, O thou that dwellest amid the praises of Israel. And one cried unto another, and said, Holy, holy, holy is the Lord of hosts : the whole earth is full of his glory. And they receive sanction the one from the other, and say Holy in the highest heavens, the place of his divine abode; holy upon earth, the work of his might ; holy for ever and to all eternity is the Lord of hosts; the whole earth is full of the radiance of his glory. Then a wind lifted me up, and I heard behind me the voice of a great rushing (saying), Blessed be the glory of the Lord from his place. Then a wind lifted me up, and I heard behind me the voice of a great rushing, of those who uttered praises, and said, Blessed be the glory of the Lord from the region of his divine abode. The Lord shall reign for ever and ever. The kingdom of the Lord endureth for ever and to all eternity. O Lord, the God of Abraham, of Isaac and of Israel, our fathers, keep this for ever in the imagination of the thoughts of the heart of thy people, and direct their heart unto thee. And he, being merciful, forgiveth iniquity and destroyeth not : yea, many a time he turneth his anger away, and doth not stir up all his wrath. For thou, O Lord, art good and forgiving, and abounding in lovingkindness to all them that call upon thee. Thy righteousness is an everlasting righteousness, and thy Law is truth. Thou wilt show truth to Jacob and lovingkindness to Abraham, according as thou hast sworn unto our fathers from the days of old. Blessed be the Lord day by day ; if one burdeneth us, God is our salvation. (Selah.) The Lord of hosts is with us; the God of Jacob is our stronghold. (Selah.) O Lord of hosts, happy is the man who trusteth in thee. Save, Lord : may the King answer us on the day when we call. Blessed is our God, who hath created us for his glory, and hath separated us from them that go astray, and hath given us the Law of truth and planted everlasting life in our midst. May he open our heart unto his Law, and place his love and fear within our hearts, that we may do his will and serve him with a perfect heart, that we may not labour in vain, nor bring forth for confusion. May it be thy will, O Lord our God and God of our fathers, that we may keep thy statutes in this world, and be worthy to live to witness and inherit happiness and blessing in the days of the Messiah and in the life of the world to come. To the end that my glory may sing praise unto thee, and not be silent : O Lord my God, I will give thanks unto thee for ever. Blessed is the man that trusteth in the Lord, and whose trust the Lord is. Trust ye in the Lord forever; for in Jah the Lord is an everlasting rock. And they that know thy name will put their trust in thee ; for thou hast not forsaken them that seek thee, Lord. It pleased the Lord, for his righteousness' sake, to magnify the Law and to make it honourable.
[JPS 1917, Ps. 8:10] O LORD, our Lord, How glorious is Thy name in all the earth! [Ps. 31:25] Be strong, and let your heart take courage, All ye that wait for the LORD.
And now, I pray thee, let the power of the Lord be great, according as thou hast spoken. Remember, O Lord, thy tender mercies and thy lovingkindnesses ; for they have been ever of old.
Reader.— Magnified and sanctified be his great name in the world which he hath created according to his will. May he establish his kingdom during your life and during your days, and during the life of all the house of Israel, even speedily and at a near time, and say ye, Amen. Cong, and Reader.— Let his great name be blessed forever and to all eternity. Reader.— Blessed, praised and glorified, exalted, extolled and honoured, magnified and lauded be the name of the Holy One, blessed be he ; though he be high above all the blessings and hymns, praises and consolations, which are uttered in the world ; and say ye, Amen. Cong.— Accept our prayer in mercy and in favour. Reader.— May the prayers and supplications of all Israel be accepted by their Father who is in heaven ; and say ye, Amen. Cong.— Let the name of the Lord be blessed from this time forth and for evermore. Reader. — May there be abundant peace from heaven, and life for us and for all Israel ; and say ye, Amen. Cong.— My help is from the Lord, who made heaven and earth. Reader.— He who maketh peace in his high places, may he make peace for us and for all Israel ; and say ye, Amen.
[JPS 1917, Ps. 86] A Prayer of David. Incline Thine ear, O LORD, and answer me; For I am poor and needy. Keep my soul, for I am godly; O Thou my God, save Thy servant that trusteth in Thee. Be gracious unto me, O Lord; For unto Thee do I cry all the day. Rejoice the soul of Thy servant; For unto Thee, O Lord, do I lift up my soul. For Thou, Lord, art good, and ready to pardon, And plenteous in mercy unto all them that call upon Thee. Give ear, O LORD, unto my prayer; And attend unto the voice of my supplications. In the day of my trouble I call upon Thee; For Thou wilt answer me. There is none like unto Thee among the gods, O Lord, And there are no works like Thine. All nations whom Thou hast made shall come and prostrate themselves before Thee, O Lord; And they shall glorify Thy name. For Thou art great, and doest wondrous things; Thou art God alone. Teach me, O LORD, Thy way, that I may walk in Thy truth; Make one my heart to fear Thy name. I will thank Thee, O Lord my God, with my whole heart; And I will glorify Thy name for evermore. For great is Thy mercy toward me; And Thou hast delivered my soul from the lowest nether-world. O God, the proud are risen up against me, And the company of violent men have sought after my soul, And have not set Thee before them. But Thou, O Lord, art a God full of compassion and gracious, Slow to anger, and plenteous in mercy and truth. O turn unto me, and be gracious unto me; Give Thy strength unto Thy servant, And save the son of Thy handmaid. Work in my behalf a sign for good; That they that hate me may see it, and be put to shame, Because Thou, LORD, hast helped me, and comforted me.
[JPS 1917, Isa. 2:5; Mic. 4:5; 1 Kgs 8:57-60] O house of Jacob, come ye, and let us walk In the light of the LORD. For let all the peoples walk each one in the name of its god, But we will walk in the name of the LORD our God for ever and ever. The LORD our God be with us, as He was with our fathers; let Him not leave us, nor forsake us; that He may incline our hearts unto Him, to walk in all His ways, and to keep His commandments, and His statutes, and His ordinances, which He commanded our fathers. And let these my words, wherewith I have made supplication before the LORD, be nigh unto the LORD our God day and night, that He maintain the cause of His servant, and the cause of His people Israel, as every day shall require; that all the peoples of the earth may know that the LORD, He is God; there is none else.
[JPS 1917, Ps. 124] A Song of Ascents; of David. 'If it had not been the LORD who was for us', Let Israel now say; 'If it had not been the LORD who was for us, When men rose up against us, Then they had swallowed us up alive, when their wrath was kindled against us; Then the waters had overwhelmed us, the stream had gone over our soul; Then the proud waters Had gone over our soul.' Blessed be the LORD, who hath not given us as a prey to their teeth. Our soul is escaped as a bird out of the snare of the fowlers; The snare is broken, and we are escaped. Our help is in the name of the LORD, Who made heaven and earth.

# Morning Prayer

<note>A decorative printer's ornament is centered at the top of the page.</note>

On the sides, regarding His return to His dwelling, it is written: For they shall see eye to eye when the Lord returns to Zion. And it is said: And the glory of the Lord shall be revealed, and all flesh shall see it together, for the mouth of the Lord has spoken. Father of Compassion, He will comfort the burdened people and remember the covenant of the mighty ancestors; He will rescue our souls from evil hours, rebuke the evil inclination from those who are carried, and grant us eternal survival. May He fulfill our requests in good measure with salvation and mercy.

<note>A decorative ornament.</note>

The Throne of Prophets, the Book of Awe, etc.
And this is the Torah which Moses placed before the children of Israel, according to the word of the Lord by the hand of Moses.

Praise the name of the Lord, for His name alone is exalted.
His glory is over earth and heaven; He has raised a horn for His people, a praise for all His pious ones, for the children of Israel, the people near to Him. Hallelujah.

And he says: In the Name standing for the generation, and it is written... <note>The text here contains cryptic abbreviations likely referring to liturgical cues or mystical permutations of the Name.</note>

And in confidence he said: Return, O Lord, to the ten thousand thousands of Israel. Arise, O Lord, to Your resting place, You and the Ark of Your strength. Let Your priests be clothed with righteousness, and let Your pious ones sing for joy. For the sake of David Your servant, do not turn away the face of Your anointed. For I have given you a good teaching; do not forsake My Torah. It is a tree of life to those who hold fast to it, and its supporters are happy. Its ways are ways of pleasantness, and all its paths are peace. Turn us back to You, O Lord, and we shall return; renew our days as of old. Happy are they...

<term>Lamnatzeach</term> <gloss>For the conductor</gloss>, a Psalm of David: May the Lord answer you in the day of distress; may the name of the God of Jacob set you on high. May He send your help from the sanctuary and support you from Zion. May He remember all your offerings and accept your burnt sacrifices. <term>Selah</term> <gloss>forever</gloss>. May He grant you according to your heart and fulfill all your counsel. We will sing for joy in Your salvation, and in the name of our God we will wave our banners; may the Lord fulfill all your requests. Now I know that the Lord saves His anointed; He answers him from His holy heavens with the saving might of His right hand. Some trust in chariots and some in horses, but we will mention the name of the Lord our God. They have bowed down and fallen, but we have risen and stand upright. O Lord, save! May the King answer us on the day we call. And a redeemer shall come to Zion and to those who turn from transgression in Jacob, says the Lord. And as for Me, this is My covenant with them, says the Lord: My spirit which is upon you, and My words which I have placed in your mouth, shall not depart from your mouth, nor from the mouth of your children, nor from the mouth of your children's children, says the Lord, from now and forever.

And You are holy, enthroned upon the praises of Israel. And one called to another and said: Holy, holy, holy is the Lord of Hosts, the whole earth is full of His glory. <note>The following is the Aramaic Targum translation of the previous verse, traditionally recited in the 'Uva Le-Tziyon' prayer.</note> And they receive word from one another and say: Holy in the highest heavens, the house of His Presence; Holy upon the earth, the work of His power; Holy forever and for all eternity. The Lord of Hosts, the whole earth is full of the radiance of His glory. Then a spirit lifted me up, and I heard behind me the voice of a great rushing: Blessed be the glory of the Lord from His place. <note>Aramaic translation follows:</note> And a spirit lifted me up, and I heard behind me a voice of great movement of those who praise and say: Blessed is the glory of the Lord from the place of the house of His Presence. The Lord shall reign forever and ever. The Lord, His kingdom stands forever and ever. O Lord, God of Abraham, Isaac, and Israel, our fathers, keep this forever as the inclination of the thoughts of the hearts of Your people, and direct their hearts toward You. And He, being merciful, forgives iniquity and does not destroy; frequently He turns away His anger and does not stir up all His wrath. For You, Lord, are good and forgiving, and abundant in kindness to all who call upon You. Your righteousness is an everlasting righteousness, and Your Torah is truth. You will give truth to Jacob and kindness to Abraham, as You have sworn to our fathers from days of old. Blessed be the Lord day by day; He carries us, the God of our salvation. <term>Selah</term>. The Lord of Hosts is with us; the God of Jacob is our stronghold. <term>Selah</term>. O Lord of Hosts, happy is the man who trusts in You. O Lord, save! May the King answer us on the day we call. Blessed is He, our God, who created us for His glory and separated us from those who go astray, and gave us a Torah of truth and planted eternal life within us. May He open our heart through His Torah and place in our heart love and awe of Him, to do His will and to serve Him with a perfect heart, so that we do not labor in vain nor give birth for terror. May it be Your will, O Lord our God and God of our fathers, that we keep Your statutes in this world, and merit to live and see and inherit goodness and blessing in the years of the Messianic age and for the life of the World to Come. So that my glory may sing to You and not be silent; O Lord my God, I will thank You forever. Blessed is the man who trusts in the Lord, and the Lord shall be his trust. Trust in the Lord forever, for in God the Lord is an everlasting Rock. And those who know Your name will trust in You, for You have not forsaken those who seek You, O Lord. The Lord desired, for the sake of His righteousness, to magnify the Torah and make it glorious.

<column-break/>

O Lord, our Master, how majestic is Your name in all the earth.
Be strong, and let your heart take courage, all you who hope in the Lord.

And now, may the power of the Lord be great, as You have spoken, saying: Remember Your mercies, O Lord, and Your kindnesses, for they are from of old.

<note>This begins the Mourner's Kaddish prayer in Aramaic.</note>
Magnified and sanctified be His great name in the world which He created according to His will. May He establish His kingdom and cause His salvation to sprout and bring near <note>alternative reading: the end/arrival of</note> His Messiah. In your lifetime and in your days and in the lifetime of the whole House of Israel, speedily and in a near time; and say, Amen. May His great name be blessed forever and to all eternity. Blessed and praised, glorified and exalted, extolled and honored, adored and lauded be the name of the Holy One, blessed be He, above <note>from time to time, and above all</note> all blessings and songs, praises and consolations that are uttered in the world; and say, Amen. Receive, receive with mercy and favor our prayer. May the prayers and supplications of the whole House of Israel be accepted before their Father who is in heaven; and say, Amen. Receive: May the name of the Lord be blessed from now and forever.

May there be abundant peace from heaven, and life upon us and upon all Israel; and say, Amen. My help is from the Lord, Maker of heaven and earth. He who makes peace in His high places, may He make peace upon us and upon all Israel; and say, Amen.

A prayer of David: Incline Your ear, O Lord, answer me, for I am poor and needy. Guard my soul, for I am pious; save Your servant who trusts in You, You are my God. Be gracious to me, O Lord, for I call to You all day long. Gladden the soul of Your servant, for to You, O Lord, I lift up my soul. For You, Lord, are good and forgiving, and abundant in kindness to all who call upon You. Give ear, O Lord, to my prayer, and listen to the voice of my supplications. In the day of my distress I call to You, for You will answer me. There is none like You among the gods, O Lord, and there are no works like Yours. All nations whom You have made shall come and bow down before You, O Lord, and shall honor Your name. For You are great and perform wonders; You alone are God. Teach me, O Lord, Your way, I will walk in Your truth; unite my heart to fear Your name. I will thank You, O Lord my God, with all my heart, and I will honor Your name forever. For Your kindness is great toward me, and You have rescued my soul from the lowest depths. O God, the arrogant have risen against me, and a company of violent men have sought my soul; they have not set You before them. But You, Lord, are a God merciful and gracious, slow to anger and abundant in kindness and truth. Turn to me and be gracious to me; give Your strength to Your servant, and save the son of Your handmaid. Work for me a sign for good, that those who hate me may see it and be ashamed, for You, O Lord, have helped me and comforted me.

House of Jacob, come and let us walk in the light of the Lord. For all the peoples walk each in the name of its god, but we will walk in the name of the Lord our God forever and ever.
May the Lord our God be with us as He was with our fathers; may He not leave us nor forsake us. To incline our hearts to Him, to walk in all His ways and to keep His commandments, His statutes, and His ordinances which He commanded our fathers. And may these words of mine, with which I have made supplication before the Lord, be near to the Lord our God day and night, that He may maintain the cause of His servant and the cause of His people Israel, as each day requires. So that all the peoples of the earth may know that the Lord is God; there is no other.

A song of ascents, by David: If the Lord had not been for us—let Israel now say—If the Lord had not been for us when man rose up against us, then they would have swallowed us alive in the heat of their anger against us. Then the waters would have overwhelmed us, the stream would have passed over our soul. Then the treacherous waters would have passed over our soul. Blessed be the Lord, who has not given us as prey to their teeth. Our soul escaped like a bird from the snare of the fowlers; the snare broke, and we escaped. Our help is in the name of the Lord, Maker of heaven and earth.

But You, Lord, are a merciful and gracious God, slow to anger and abounding in kindness and truth. Work in my behalf a sign for good, that those who hate me may see it and be put to shame, because You, Lord, have helped me and comforted me.

O House of Jacob, come and let us walk in the light of the Lord. For all the peoples walk each in the name of its god, but we will walk in the name of the Lord our God forever and ever. May the Lord our God be with us as He was with our ancestors; may He not leave us nor forsake us. To incline our hearts to Him, to walk in all His ways and to keep His commandments, His statutes, and His ordinances which He commanded our ancestors. And let these words of mine, with which I have made supplication before the Lord, be near to the Lord our God day and night, that He may maintain the cause of His servant and the cause of His people Israel, as each day requires. So that all the peoples of the earth may know that the Lord is God; there is none else.

A Song of Ascents, of David: If it had not been the Lord who was on our side—let Israel now say—If it had not been the Lord who was on our side when men rose up against us, then they would have swallowed us up alive, when their anger was kindled against us. Then the waters would have overwhelmed us, the stream would have gone over our soul. Then the proud waters would have gone over our soul. Blessed be the Lord, who has not given us as prey to their teeth. Our soul has escaped as a bird out of the snare of the fowlers; the snare is broken, and we have escaped. Our help is in the name of the Lord, the Maker of heaven and earth.

For the conductor, a psalm of David: May the Lord answer you in the day of distress; may the name of the God of Jacob set you on high. May he send your help from the sanctuary and support you from Zion. May he remember all your meal offerings and accept your burnt sacrifices, Selah. May he grant you according to your heart and fulfill all your counsel. We will sing for joy in your salvation, and in the name of our God we will set up our banners; may the Lord fulfill all your petitions. Now I know that the Lord saves his anointed; he will answer him from his holy heaven with the saving strengths of his right hand. O Lord, save; may the King answer us in the day we call. And a redeemer shall come to Zion and to those who turn from transgression in Jacob, says the Lord. And as for me, this is my covenant with them, says the Lord: My spirit which is upon you, and my words which I have put in your mouth, shall not depart from your mouth, nor from the mouth of your offspring, nor from the mouth of your offspring's offspring, says the Lord, from now and forever.

[context] This great Abasside
is extremely kind towards the Jews, many of his officers being of that nation; he understands all languages, is well versed in the mosaic law and reads and writes the hebrew language.
He enjoys nothing, but what he earns by the labour of his own hands and therefore manufactures coverlets which he stamps with his seal and which his officers sell in the public market; these articles are purchased by the nobles of the land and from their produce his necessaries are provided.
The Khalif is an excellent man, trustworthy and kind-hearted towards every one, but generally invisible to the mahomedans. The pilgrims, which come hither from distant countries on their way to Mekha in Yemen, desire to be presented to him and thus address him from the palace: 'Our Lord, light of the mahomedans and splendor of our religion, show us the brightness of thy countenance', but he heeds not their words. His servants and officers then approach and pray: 'O Lord, manifest thy peace to those men, who come from distant lands and desire shelter in the shadow of thy glory' and after such petition he rises and puts one corner of his garment out of the window,
[context] which is eagerly kissed by the pilgrims.

דזיוו — כלהו לוקמוהי. **רבי אלעזר** סח ליצחק מנו דיכא קטיא כפף דקה יצחק דיכא קטיא חמיל לחולקיה ח"ו רגז ולא הוה כחולקיה והא יצחק מנו חסד כפחא וק' כי כלהו דינא מנו רחמי כפחא ורחמי מליכא. חכרה ירית לחסדא דחסד כפף ויצחק כדינא מנו חסד יצחק כפף ברחמי מנו דינא קשיא ובך הוה לעילא דא מן דא ונפק ליה מן דא עד דאשתמודע כלא דכהא חד ומהד תליין כלהו וכלא לאשתכח חד צריך שמיא לעלם ולעלמי עלמין. **רבי אלעזר** אסתמודע דלית סרטין דל לה כד חזינן לה כדא וחד חמיד בתרווייהו לסכללא כלא כגון יעקב והיינו דכתיב:
> מברח מן הקצה אל הקצה <note>שמות כו:כח</note>

תוכח כלי דאי לא תקרי אלא מסטרא דילן ומסטרא דילן אשתמודע כלא כהו יכילא כלא בחד מתקלא סלקא לא שכי ולא ישתני כמה דכתיב:
> אני יי' לא שניתי <note>מלאכי ג:ו</note>

**רבי יהודה** כלהון כוסיפין נהירין מהד ומהד תליין וכונניו היכהו חד כלא ולא לאתפרשא ומאן דפריש לון בחיליה אתפרש מן חיי עלמין. **רבי יצחק** כתיב:
> ונתתי נערים שריהם ותעלולים ימשלו בם <note>ישעיהו ג:ד</note>

היינו דכתיב ועזים פנים כרובים ודא וכתיב יושב הכרובים וכתיב וירכב על כרוב ויעף. יושב הכרובים כד שריא לאתיישבא בסיועותא כתיב יושב הכרובים (דא כד אשתכח בשלימותא) וירכב על כרוב חד דלא אתיישבא מלכא בכרסייה. יושב הכרובים תרי. לדייפי ווי לעלמא כד חד כרוב להדר אנפי מתבריא דהא כתיב:
> ופניהם איש אל אחיו <note>שמות כה:כ</note>

כד הוו שלמא בעלמא. **רבי יצחק** קל תנינן ערוה לבין ונערות חמך לא תגלה ווי למאן דגלי עריתהון כגוונא דא כתיב ביעקב מברח מן הקצה אל הקצה. וכהא חולקהון דישראל לקודשא בריך הוא אשתכח בתכשיטייהו כגוונא דלעילא דכתיב:
> ישראל אשר בך אתפאר <note>ישעיהו מט:ג</note>

תא חזי **רבי יצחק** ביומי קדמוהי הוי כד חד אמר לחבריה חומא לי מנא חדא וטול מנה כסף. השתא אמר בר נש לחבריה טול מנה כסף ואחמתלא בחוריתא ולית מין דיטעם ולית מאן דירכון חולכיה בר חיכון זעירין קליטין עלינין לקודשא בריך הוא אשתכח כהו דכתיב:
> ועמך כלם צדיקים לעולם ירשו ארץ נצר מטעי מעשה ידי להתפאר <note>ישעיהו ס:כא</note>

ווי דיתמליס ומתקיימא כסף. **רבי יצחק** אמר ווי כי נמולים קא חמינא כל חינון דמתתאלן מקטרי קיימין עלאין חקרון ווי דיתמליס וכל חיכון לנתתא תליין חחיכון ווי. חלונותא פתח בנו פתח ומתחלדן ומתתקנין מקוטרא לסדרא דקחיס עלייהו. וכספרא דכביעותא תוכח ווי לעילא ווי לתתא וכלהו במתקלא חד סלקין. מאן דביעותא דספרא **אמר רבי חזקיה** פרקין חינון דכולהן בהיכל רב ומליין כל ארעא. **רבי יהודה** חי כולהן הכי מכהו עדיפי. **אמר רבי** קבי הוי למאן דעט וכפף ולמאן דלא עלה וכפף להו הכי.

---

### The Parable of the Wheat

מתלא לבר נש דהוה דיירין ביני דברין ולא ידע בדיורי מתא. וזרע חטין ואכל חטין כגופייהו. יומא חד עאל למתא לקריבוסו כקמא טבא. אמר מהא בר נש דכא למה. אמרו כקמא הוא למיכל. אכל וטעם אחלא למכיה. **אמר רבי** מרוממא דא עביד דא. אמרו חטין. לבתר דקריבוסו גרונין דליסין במתחא. טעם מכיהו אמר וחלינומתא התנבידי. אמרו חטין. לבתר דקריבונו טריקי מלכין דליסין בדובשא ומשחא. אמר וחלויין חמת עבידו. אמרו חטין. אמר ודאי חכא מחרי לכל חלין דהכא חכיל עקרא דכל חלין דהיכו חטי. ובגין ההוא...

Said R. Eleazar: ‘It would seem that Jacob emanated from the region of severe Judgement, for Isaac laid hold on this attribute as his portion.’ Said R. Simeon to him: ‘But was this the only grade? Isaac emanated from Grace, surely, and so did all the Fathers. In fact, Judgement proceeds from Mercy, and Mercy from Judgement. Abraham inherited Mercy, and Isaac proceeded therefrom, but with the aura of Judgement about him; and Jacob in turn issued in Mercy from the midst of Judgement. So one quality emanates from another, each imbibes from each, and finally it is made manifest that all are one, and all depend on One, and the One is all in all. Blessed be His Name for ever and ever.’
Said R. Eleazar: ‘It is evident that there can be no perfection except the one aspect be joined to the other and a third hold them together to harmonize and complete them, like Jacob in relation to Abraham and Isaac. That is why it is written: “And the middle bar in the midst of the boards shall be fastening from one end to the other.”
We have been taught that all this differentiation of the Divine Personality is from our side and relative to our knowledge, and that, above, all is one, all is set in one balance, unvarying and eternal, as it is written: “I the Lord change not” (Mal. 3, 6).’ Said R. Judah: ‘All the heavenly lights are illumined from one and depend on one, and all the lights there form only one Light, and desire never to be separated, and he who does separate them in his mind is as though he separated himself from life eternal.’
Said R. Isaac: ‘It is written, “And I will give youths to be their princes, and babes shall rule over them” (Isa. 3, 4). This is an allusion to the words, “And thou shalt make two cherubims of gold” (Ex. 25, 18). It is also written: “The ark of the Lord which dwelleth between the cherubims” (I Sam. 4, 4); and again it is written, “And he rode upon a cherub” (2 Sam. 22, 11). When He dwells in completeness, He “dwelleth between cherubims”, but when the King is not established on His Throne, He “rides” on “one” cherub.
Said R. Jose: ‘Woe unto the world when one cherub turns away his face from the other, for it is written, “And their faces shall look one to another” (Ex. 25, 20); only then is there harmony in the world.’ Said R. Isaac: ‘We have been taught that the words, “The nakedness of thy father, or the nakedness of thy mother, shalt thou not uncover” (Lev. 18, 7) have an esoteric reference to supermundane relationships in addition to their obvious significance. Woe to him who “uncovers their nakedness” (by probing too deeply into the hidden mysteries of the inner aspects of the Divine Essence and the relationship of one to another). Similarly, it is written in regard to Jacob: “fastening from one end to the other”. Happy is the lot of Israel, by whose praises the Holy One, blessed be He, is glorified even as He is glorified above: “Israel in whom I am glorified” (Isa. 49, 3).’
We have been taught that R. Isaac once said: ‘In bygone times a person used to say to his neighbour, “Speak to me on a certain portion of the Torah and I will pay thee for it”; but in our days, even if one person says to another, “Study the Torah and I will reward thee with money for so doing”, no one inclines his ears to listen, and none desires knowledge except those few saints of the Highest in whom the Holy One is glorified, and concerning whom it is written, “And thy people shall be all righteous, they shall inherit the land for ever, the branch of my planting, the work of my hands, that I may be glorified” (Ibid. 60, 21).’
THE HOOKS OF THE PILLARS AND THEIR FILLETS SHALL BE OF SILVER. Said R. Isaac: ‘I presume that the “hooks of the pillars” symbolize all those who are attached to the supernal unifying pillars, and that all those who are below depend on them. What is the significance of the word vavim (hooks; also the letter vau, the numerical value of which is six)? Six within six (vv), all united and nourished by the Spine which is set over them. And we have learnt in the Book of the Hidden Mystery (Sifra di-zenintha) this dictum: “Hooks above, hooks below (six above, six below), all comprehended in one meaning and one name, having one and the same significance.”
Now, what is this “Book of the Hidden Mystery”?’ Said R. Simeon: ‘It contains five sections which are to be found in the midst of a great Hall, and whose wisdom fills the whole earth.’ Said R. Judah: ‘If this book of wisdom is enclosed in that Hall, it is of more worth than any other tome.’ ‘Verily,’ returned R. Simeon, ‘it is so, for one who is used to passing in and out of the courts of wisdom, but not to one who rarely or never enters into that Hall.
Once there was a man who dwelt among the mountains and was a complete stranger to the ways of townsfolk. He sowed wheat, but knew no better than to consume it in its natural condition. One day he went down into a city, and there a loaf of good bread was placed before him. He asked what it was, and was informed that it was bread and was meant to eat. He ate it and liked it. “What is it made of?” he said. They told him “Wheat”. Later, he was given fine cake kneaded in oil. He tasted it, and again asked: “And this, of what is it made?” The same reply was made as before: “Of wheat”. Finally, he was treated to some royal confectionery, flavoured with oil and honey. Once more he asked his question, and obtained the same reply. Then he said: “In sooth, I have all these at my command, because I eat the essential constituent of all, namely wheat.”
[context] Thus, through his untutored taste he remained a stranger to all these delicious flavours, and their enjoyment was lost to him.

## Main Text (Zohar)

Of the radiance—they have all established it. **Rabbi Eleazar** spoke to Isaac: who is the <term>deika katya</term> <gloss>broken spirit</gloss>? Isaac bowed his head. Isaac was <term>deika katya</term> <gloss>broken in spirit</gloss>, he was concerned for his portion; Heaven forbid he should be angry, for his portion was not like the others. And behold, Isaac is from the side of <term>Chesed</term> <gloss>Mercy/Kindness</gloss>, yet it is bent? And it is asked: for all of them are <term>Din</term> <gloss>Judgment</gloss>, yet he is from <term>Rachamim</term> <gloss>Compassion</gloss>, and <term>Rachamim</term> <gloss>Compassion</gloss> is the King. Wisdom inherits <term>Chesed</term> <gloss>Mercy</gloss>, for <term>Chesed</term> <gloss>Mercy</gloss> bows, and Isaac as <term>Din</term> <gloss>Judgment</gloss> is from <term>Chesed</term> <gloss>Mercy</gloss>. Isaac bows in <term>Rachamim</term> <gloss>Compassion</gloss>, from which comes harsh <term>Din</term> <gloss>Judgment</gloss>. And thus it was above, this from that, and it emerged from this until that, until all was recognized as one. And all depend on one another, and for all to be found as one, the Heavens are needed forever and ever. **Rabbi Eleazar** recognized that there are no paths for it when we see it as such, and one is desired in both of them to complete everything, such as Jacob, and this is what is written: 
> passing through from end to end <note>Exodus 26:28</note>

The proof is everything, for if you only read from our side and from our side, everything is recognized as being able to rise in one <term>matkala</term> <gloss>balance/scale</gloss>; it does not change or shift, as it is written:
> I am the Lord, I change not <note>Malachi 3:6</note>

**Rabbi Yehuda** said: all of them are radiant cups, depending on one another, and their foundations are as one, all of it, and they are not to be separated. And whoever separates them by his strength is separated from the life of the worlds. **Rabbi Isaac** said: it is written:
> And I will give children to be their princes, and babes shall rule over them <note>Isaiah 3:4</note>

This is what is written regarding the "brazen-faced" <term>Keruvim</term> <gloss>Cherubim</gloss>, and this is what is written, "He who sits upon the Cherubim," and it is written, "And He rode upon a Cherub and did fly." "He who sits upon the Cherubim" refers to when He begins to dwell in assistance; it is written "He who sits upon the Cherubim" <note>this is when He is found in perfection</note>. "And He rode upon a Cherub" <note>singular</note> refers to when the King does not dwell upon His throne. "He who sits upon the Cherubim" <note>plural</note> is two. Woe to the world when one Cherub turns its face away, for it is written:
> and their faces shall look one to another <note>Exodus 25:20</note>

This is when there was peace in the world. **Rabbi Isaac** said: we have learned, "the nakedness of a daughter-in-law and the youth of your father-in-law you shall not uncover." Woe to one who uncovers their nakedness. In this manner it is written of Jacob: "passing through from end to end." And thus the portion of Israel with the Holy One, Blessed be He, is found in their ornaments, in the manner of that which is above, as it is written:
> Israel, in whom I will be glorified <note>Isaiah 49:3</note>

Come and see, **Rabbi Isaac** said: in former days, when one said to his fellow, "Show me one vessel and take money for it." Now a man says to his fellow, "Take money from me and show me another," and there is no one to taste it and no one to incline his portion, except for those few who are gathered and high unto the Holy One, Blessed be He, as it is written:
> And your people shall all be righteous; they shall inherit the land forever, the branch of my planting, the work of my hands, that I may be glorified <note>Isaiah 60:21</note>

Woe that the money is fulfilled and sustained. **Rabbi Isaac** said: Woe, for I see those who are circumcised, all those who are crowned from the higher knots, they search. Woe that it is fulfilled, and all those who depend below, woe. A window opens within us, opening and being renewed and prepared from the smoke to the order that takes pity on them. And as in the Book of Concealment <note>original: Sifra De-Tzniuta</note> it is proven: woe above, woe below, and all of them rise in one balance. Who is the fear of the book? **Rabbi Hezekiah said**: these sections are all in the Great Palace and fill the whole earth. **Rabbi Yehuda** said: all of them are superior in this way. **Rabbi said**: Woe to the one who deviates and bows, and to the one who does not ascend and bow to them in this way.

### The Parable of the Wheat

A parable of a man who dwelt among the fields and did not know the ways of the city dwellers. He sowed wheat and ate the wheat as it was <note>raw kernels</note>. One day he entered the city, and they brought him a good loaf of bread. He said: what is this man eating? They said: it is bread to eat. He ate and found it very tasty. **The Rabbi said**: This is made from greatness. They said: it is wheat. Later they brought him cakes kneaded in oil. He tasted them and said: surely these are exquisite. They said: they are wheat. Later they brought him royal pastries made with honey and oil. He said: and these sweets, how are they made? They said: they are wheat. He said: certainly I am the master of all these things, for I eat the essence of all these, which is wheat. And because of that...

Of the radiance — all of them have established its meaning. **Rabbi Eleazar** spoke to Isaac: Who is this "diminished male" <note>original: "dekha katya"</note>? Isaac bowed. Isaac was thin and concerned for his portion; Heaven forbid he should become angry, for his portion would not remain. And yet, is Isaac not characterized by Mercy <term>Chesed</term>? <note>The text explores the tension between Isaac's traditional association with Judgment and the flow of Mercy.</note> Because all is Judgment <term>Din</term>, it is drawn from Mercy <term>Rachamim</term>, and Mercy comes from the King. Wisdom inherits Mercy, for Mercy bows, and Isaac as Judgment is drawn from Mercy. Isaac bows before Mercy, though from him comes harsh Judgment. So it was above, one from the other, and it issued from this one until that one, until all was known as one. All are dependent on one another, and for all to be found as one, the Heavens are needed forever and ever.

**Rabbi Eleazar** perceived that there are no markings for it except when we see it as one. One is desired in both of them to complete the whole, like Jacob <note>who represents the middle pillar balancing Mercy and Judgment</note>. This is what is written:
> passing through from end to end <note>Exodus 26:28</note>

This proves the whole. If you do not read it but from this side and that side, all is known. All can be contained in one balance <term>matkala</term>; it does not deviate and does not change, as it is written:
> I am the Lord, I change not <note>Malachi 3:6</note>

**Rabbi Judah** said: All these lights are illuminated by one another and depend on one another. They are established as one whole, never to be separated. Whoever separates them by his own strength is separated from the Life of Worlds. **Rabbi Isaac** said: It is written:
> And I will give children to be their princes, and babes shall rule over them <note>Isaiah 3:4</note>

This refers to what is written regarding "brazen-faced" Cherubim <term>Keruvim</term>. It is written, "He who sits upon the Cherubim," and it is written, "He rode upon a Cherub and did fly." "He who sits upon the Cherubim" occurs when the indwelling is established in support <note>in a state of completeness</note>. "He rode upon a Cherub" <note>singular</note> refers to when the King is not established upon His throne. "He who sits upon the Cherubim" <note>plural</note> refers to two. Woe to the world when one Cherub turns its face away from the other! For it is written:
> with their faces one toward another <note>Exodus 25:20</note>

This occurs when there is peace in the world. **Rabbi Isaac** said: We have learned: Do not uncover the nakedness of a daughter-in-law or a youth. Woe to the one who uncovers their nakedness! In this manner, it is written of Jacob that he "passed through from end to end." So too the portion of Israel with the Holy One, blessed be He, is found in their adornments, just as it is above, as it is written:
> Israel, in whom I will be glorified <note>Isaiah 49:3</note>

Come and see, **Rabbi Isaac** said: In former days, if a man said to his fellow, "Show me a single vessel and take silver for it," he would. Now, a man says to his fellow, "Take silver and show me another," but there is no one to taste it and no one to incline his portion, except for a few select ones, supreme before the Holy One, blessed be He. About them it is written:
> Your people shall all be righteous; they shall inherit the land forever, the branch of my planting, the work of my hands, that I may be glorified <note>Isaiah 60:21</note>

Woe that silver should be so depleted and yet endure. **Rabbi Isaac** said: Woe, for I see those who are circumcised, all those who are crowned and stand in the higher heights. Woe that they are depleted, for all those below depend on those above. Woe! A window was opened for us, and they are renewed and prepared from the smoke in the order that rests upon them. As it is proven in the Book of Concealment <term>Sifra Detzniuta</term>: Woe above, woe below, for all of them rise in one balance. Who is the fear of the Book? **Rabbi Hezekiah said**: These chapters are all in the Great Palace <term>Heikhal</term> and fill the whole earth. **Rabbi Judah** said: All of them are even greater than this. **Rabbi** said: Woe to the one who deviates and bows, and to the one who does not ascend and bow before them.

### The Parable of the Wheat

A parable of a man who lived in the fields and did not know of the dwellers of the city. He sowed wheat and ate wheat in its raw form. One day he entered the city, and they brought before him a good bread. He said: "What is this man eating?" They said: "It is bread to eat." He ate and found it very pleasant to his taste. **The Rabbi said**: "From what is this made?" They said: "Wheat." Later they brought before him cakes kneaded in oil. He tasted them and said: "And what are these made of?" They said: "Wheat." Later they brought before him the royal pastries kneaded with honey and oil. He said: "And what are these delicacies made of?" They said: "Wheat." He said: "Surely I am the master of all these things here, for I eat the essence of all these, which is wheat." Then I said to the Kadi : “ And knowest thou his father? may Allah put him to shame!” He replied : “ How should Abu Zayd be unknown for whose wound there is no retaliation, and of whom every Kadi has stories to tell and proclamation to make.” Then I gnashed my teeth in anger and said, “ There is no power and no strength, but in Allah, the Exalted, the Great,” becoming wide awake, but when the time had slipped, and making sure that his face-veil was a net of his cunning, and the crowning couplet of his poem. So my mishap made me cast down my looks, and I swore that I would never again deal with the bearer of a face-veil as long as I lived, bewailing all the while my losing bargain, and the shame to which I should be put amongst my comrades. Then the Kadi said to me, when he saw my distress, and became clearly aware of the brunt of my burning grief: “ Ay such a one, thy loss has given thee a lesson, and he who has roused [awakened] thy wits, has not done thee an injury ; take then warning by thy adventure and conceal from thy friends what has befallen thee; remember always what has occurred to thee, so as to keep in mind the admonition which thy money has administered thee and mould thyself after the disposition of one who has been tried and shown patience and who has profited by the examples set before him.” Said Al Harith, son of Hammam : Thereupon I took leave from him, donning the raiment of shame and sorrow and trailing my skirt of defrauded folly, and I purposed to show Abu Zayd my aversion by shunning him,

It was then that I shaved <note>likely referring to a ritual act or a sign of completion</note> and regained my senses, but only after the opportunity had passed. I became certain that this whole affair was a wicked plot and a mere poetic device. What I encountered caused my gaze to fall in shame. I swore an oath that I would never deal with the likes of those two for as long as I remained alive. Then I did not cease moaning over my failed transaction and my public exposure among my companions.

When the judge saw what had happened to me, and the freedom of the situation had clearly passed, he said to me: "O you! None of your wealth is truly gone if it served to warn you. He who awakened you did not commit a crime against you. So, take a lesson from what has come to you, and let your companions see what befell you. You will always remember what struck you, so that the memory of your lost dirhams <gloss>silver coins</gloss> may pass away, and there may be renewed in you the spirit of one who was tested and showed patience, and to whom the moral became clear, so he took heed."

I bid him farewell, not asking out of shame and sadness, trailing the hem of my loss and deception. I intended to confront Abu Zayd openly with the news, speaking with total frankness.

[context] Dimna instantly replied, that there were several impediments to the good administration of public affairs which might be mentioned; for instance, favouritism, which founded generally on caprice or some worse motive, gives the reins of government into feeble if not polluted hands, to the proscription of those faithful counsellors of a nation, who have courage to refuse becoming the tools of the passions of the prince : another evil of the body politic is that animosity of parties, which is continually keeping up a petty warfare in the state :
a third source of mischief is a profligacy of manners, when respect for decency in the prince and the higher circles has fled before the fascinating and authorized display of female attractions, and the severity of business is lulled to sleep in the lap of luxurious amusement and excess : the prevalence of these disorders gives rise to and nurtures those unfeeling and inhuman passions, by which calumny is engendered, and the tongue sends forth its venom to taint the bliss and satisfaction of conspicuous worth ; or the arm is lifted up to acts of violence and oppression; or dangers arise from the practice of severity where gentleness was called for ; or of indulgence when severity would have been a virtue ; or, lastly, the hand of time becomes visible in the age and infirmities of the sovereign, or in his exposure to the plagues of famine or war; and the conduct of the lion, continued he, in the preference which he has shewn to the bull, will prove in all probability a source of some of the dangers which I have enumerated. Granted, replied Kalila, but how will you contrive to get the better of the bull, considering the reputation which he enjoys. You seem to draw your conclusions, answered Dimna, from the apparent weakness of my person, compared with that of the bull, without reflecting that bodily force is not always the criterion of success; on the contrary, contrivance and skill have been often known to succeed where the greatest exertion of strength would have failed, as was exemplified by the manner in which a crow destroyed a serpent, as related in the following story. A crow had made her nest in a tree upon a mountain, at no great distance from which was the hole of a serpent ; and the serpent, as soon as the crow had hatched her young, came and took them away, and ate them. This very much distressed the crow, who went and made her complaint to a jackal, who was her friend, and asked his opinion of what she proposed to do, which was, when the serpent was asleep, to put out his eyes, and get rid of her enemy. The jackal did not at all approve of this plan, but advised the crow to think of some other method, which would be attended with less danger; because if she proceeded as she had mentioned, she might possibly experience the fate of the swan, who perished in his attempt to kill a crab.
