For one who has a portion in the holy people must show [himself] greater than all in faith, to receive the guests, to rejoice in this world and in the world to come. And a person must bring joy to the poor, because the portion of those guests that he invites belongs to the poor. And he who sits in the fullness of faith and invites these supernal guests, the guests of faith, and gives them their portion—they all stand before him and say:
> **Do not eat the bread of him who has an evil eye, etc.** <note>Proverbs 23:6</note>

It is found that such a table which he prepared is his own, and not the Holy One, blessed be He’s. Concerning him it is written:
> **I will spread dung upon your faces, the dung of your festival sacrifices, etc.** <note>Malachi 2:3</note>

Woe to that person when those guests of faith rise from the table. And Rabbi Abba said: Abraham, all his days, would stand at the crossroads to invite guests and to prepare a table for them. Now that they invite him, and all the righteous, and King <term>David</term>, and they are not given their portion, this is the hardest of all, and it is called:
> **Depart, I pray you, from the tents of these wicked men.** <note>Numbers 16:26</note>

And they all go up and say: <term>Isaac</term> says:
> **But the belly of the wicked shall want.** <note>Proverbs 13:25</note>

<term>Jacob</term> says:
> **The morsel which you have eaten, you shall vomit up.** <note>Proverbs 23:8</note>

And all the rest of the righteous say:
> **For all tables are full of filthy vomit, so that there is no place clean.** <note>Isaiah 28:8</note>

King <term>David</term> says—and the laws of oppression [apply]—as it is written: "And it was like the lead of the seas," and "The Lord shall wave," regarding all. And when does he strike? Because <term>David</term> felt the lack, and he was made a guest, but [the host] did not desire him, nor invite him, nor give him his portion. Since the Crown and the Right Hand of King <term>David</term> push the world away from that person who deprived him of his portion more than all. Rather, the first of everything belongs to the guests. And if he gives to the guests and the Holy One, blessed be He, rejoices with him, he calls upon him the blessing:
> **Then shall you delight yourself in the Lord, etc.** <note>Isaiah 58:14</note>

And <term>Isaac</term> calls upon him:
> **No weapon that is formed against you shall prosper.** <note>Isaiah 54:17</note>

Rabbi Shimon said: This King <term>David</term> says it, because all the weapons of the King and the battles of the King were entrusted into the hands of <term>David</term>. Therefore, "whoever rejoices being a hero in his portion and his will, etc." <term>Jacob</term> said to him: "And your light shall break forth as the morning, etc." The rest of the righteous said: "And the Lord shall guide you continually, and satisfy, etc." King <term>David</term> said: "No weapon that is formed against you shall prosper," for he is appointed over all kinds of weapons. And all this portion of a person who merits all these merits, the portion of the righteous in this world and in the world to come, concerning them it is written:
> **Your people also shall be all righteous, etc.** <note>Isaiah 60:21</note>

### The Faithful Shepherd (<term>Ra'aya Meheimna</term>)

-> **And you shall take for yourselves on the first day, etc.** <- <note>Leviticus 23:40</note>

**This commandment** is to take the <term>lulav</term> as is proper in these days, and let them be humble and arm themselves. And the secret that we have established is "and you shall take" <term>pederos</term> [an honor], just as the Holy One, blessed be He, takes Israel at this time of judgment. So too, they should seek the Holy One, blessed be He, in their portion and take refuge in Him. And first, this <term>lulav</term> is prepared to take the secret of the image of Man, and so below.

The creation [was] through His mercies and His laws, even His deeds. All the creation is Man, whom the Holy One, blessed be He, called by His name, as it is written: "And God created Man in His own image." And furthermore, he is called by His name at the time when Truth and Radiance emerge in the world, and he is called God, as it is written: "You shall not revile God." He called him by His name, as it is written: "And God created

---

Man in His own image." And we have established it well, as it is written: **"Let us make man in our image, after our likeness,"** which was said at the time of the [divine] union. And such is the intention of both, in image and likeness, and from the union of male and female emerged "And God created Man in His own image." Just as the King ascended, we find that at the time of the union, he was found.

When with the palatable food he'd done, the king sought wine, began a joyous bout.
When sundry cups of wine the king had drunk, the perspiration started from his brow.
He said, O host, who own (this) golden house, your place is pleasant, and your means are good.
But this high palace (here) of sixty steps, around whose head the sky its lasso whirls, —
When sixty years have now passed over you, how can you walk up to the top of it?
The officer replied, The King live aye! His wine be Kausar, huris give the cup!
This is in me no wonder, I'm a man; how should I (then) be wearied by such steps?
The wonder this, that there's a moon-like girl, soft, dainty as the king's ermine and silk.
Who puts a mount-like ox upon her back, and brings it hither at the feeding-time.
She bears it sixty steps up at a stretch, not resting (on the way) at any step.
An ox! What ox? An elephant, a load which ne'er an elephant would bear a mile.
God witness! in this land no one could (lift and) poise it for a moment from the ground.
Then (if) a woman bears it to a height of sixty steps, is it not marvellous?
After the officer had told this tale, the king bit with his teeth his finger-tips.
He said, How can a thing of this kind be? It cannot; if it be, 'tis sorcery.
This business I, in truth, shall not believe, until with my own eyes I see it (done).
Then of (his) host, (the officer), he asked that he should prove the claim his words set forth.
The host heard this; he went below and told to her who bore the ox the lion's case.

“If you do not want a gem such as this,
a lady desired by many lords of men,
then what manner of theory, <j>precepts and vows, livelihood,
and rebirth in a new life do you assert?”
“After judging among the teachings,”
said the Buddha to Māgaṇḍiya,
“none have been adopted thinking, ‘I assert this.’
Seeing views without adopting any,
searching, I saw inner peace.”
“O sage, you speak of judgments you have formed,”
said Māgaṇḍiya,
“without having adopted any of those views.
As to that matter of ‘inner peace’—
how is that described by the attentive?”
“Purity is spoken of not as due to view,”
said the Buddha to Māgaṇḍiya,
“learning, knowledge, or precepts and vows;
nor without view, learning,
knowledge, or precepts and vows.
Having relinquished these, not adopting them,
peaceful, independent, one would not pray <j>for another life.”
“It seems purity is spoken of not as due to view,”
said Māgaṇḍiya,
“learning, knowledge, or precepts and vows;
nor without view, learning,
knowledge, or precepts and vows.

### Chapter of the Octads <note>original: "Atthakavagga"</note>

836. <note>Magandiya speaks:</note> If you do not desire such a jewel, a woman sought after by many lords of men, then what kind of belief <note>original: "diṭṭhigataṃ"</note>, what kind of life governed by rules and vows, and what kind of rebirth do you proclaim?

837. <note>The Blessed One </note><note>original: "Bhagavā"</note> speaks: Magandiya, such a person does not have a thought of "I proclaim this" based on anything grasped after making a judgment among doctrines. Looking among various beliefs and not grasping any of them, I saw inward peace <note>original: "ajjhattasanti"</note> while searching.

838. <note>Magandiya speaks:</note> Those settled conclusions which have been imagined, O Sage <note>original: "muni"</note>, you say you do not grasp them. This matter which you call "inward peace," how is that explained by the wise?

839. <note>The Blessed One speaks:</note> Magandiya, I do not say that purity comes by means of belief, or by what is heard, or by knowledge, or even by rules and vows. Nor does it come from the absence of belief, the absence of hearing, the absence of knowledge, or the absence of rules and vows. Abandoning these without grasping, being at peace and not depending on anything, one would not crave for renewed existence.

840. <note>Magandiya speaks:</note> If you indeed say that purity does not come by means of belief, nor by what is heard, nor by knowledge, nor even by rules and vows...

# The Chapter of Eights <note>original: Atthakavagga</note>

836. "If you do not desire such a jewel as this," <note>Magandiya refers to his beautiful daughter, whom he offered to the Buddha.</note> "a woman sought after by many lords of men, then what kind of belief, what conduct and vows, and what sort of future rebirth do you proclaim?" <margin>Magandiya speaks</margin>

837. "I do not say 'I proclaim this' based on things taken up after making a judgment among various doctrines," said the Blessed One <note>original: Bhagava</note> to Magandiya. "But searching among the various views and not grasping them, I saw inward peace."

838. "Those very judgments that have been fashioned," said Magandiya, "you speak of them, Sage, without grasping them. This matter which you call 'inward peace,' how is that explained by the wise?"

839. "Not by means of views, nor by learning, nor by knowledge," said the Blessed One to Magandiya, "nor even by conduct and vows does one attain purity. Neither is it attained by the absence of views, the absence of learning, the absence of knowledge, or the absence of conduct and vows. Letting go of these without grasping, being at peace and not depending on anything, one would not crave for becoming <note>original: bhava; the cycle of rebirth</note>."

840. "If you indeed say that purity is not by views, nor by learning, nor by knowledge," said Magandiya, "nor even by conduct and vows..."
